skill.name: budget-pacing-monitor
skill.description: Monitor in-flight advertising spend against an even, front-loaded, or back-loaded target curve. Identify pacing gaps and decide whether to hold or reassess budget.
skill.summary: Compare campaign spend with its planned curve and identify reallocation triggers.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Thirty-four static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed repository links, benign GitHub metadata, and ordinary campaign terminology. The line 57 alert is confirmed because the skill directs execution of a Python ledger command with an unquoted campaign placeholder. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The ledger command includes a user-provided campaign value as an unquoted shell argument.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the campaign identifier and invoke ledger.py with a structured argument array instead of shell interpolation.

content.value_statement: Campaign spend can drift from planned pacing before teams notice overdelivery or stalled delivery. This skill compares spend with a target curve and recommends when to hold or reassess budget.
actual_capabilities: Compares cumulative campaign spend with even, front-loaded, or back-loaded target curves.
Calculates percent-to-pace and projects end-of-flight spend for lifetime budgets.
Classifies delivery as On-track, Ahead, Behind, or Stalled.
Checks learning-phase status before recommending budget action.
Separates observed pacing gaps from plausible delivery causes.
Produces a fire-or-hold trigger with the deciding band and next check date.
limitations: Requires accurate spend data, budget details, flight dates, and a target curve.
Does not calculate a new allocation, choose a bid strategy, or score account quality.
Projections assume the current spending rate and may change with future delivery conditions.
Cannot confirm a delivery cause when the campaign export lacks relevant fields.

use_cases.title: Check a live campaign
use_cases.description: Review current spend against plan before changing daily caps or audience settings.

use_cases.title: Review portfolio delivery
use_cases.description: Identify campaigns that need attention during a weekly performance review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a client pacing report
use_cases.description: Explain measured pacing, projected spend, likely drivers, and the next decision point.

prompt_templates.title: Check basic pacing
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Campaign X pacing. Budget is $6,000 for 30 days, 9 days elapsed, and measured spend is $2,100. Use an even curve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check using a single spend snapshot.

prompt_templates.title: Assess delivery status
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this daily spend export against an even curve. Confirm learning status, calculate percent-to-pace, classify delivery, and recommend fire or hold.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with campaign export data.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a pacing change
prompt_templates.prompt: Spend increased after day 10. Compare daily spend with the front-loaded plan, separate observed changes from likely causes, and set the next check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed diagnosis of a mid-flight change.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a reallocation trigger
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supplied target curve and trigger band. Project final spend, assess learning risk, identify the delivery driver, and prepare a handoff when triggered.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced decision support with explicit operating rules.

output_examples.input: Campaign X: $6,000 budget, 30 days, day 9, $2,100 measured spend, even curve, and an 85% to 120% pacing band.
output: Measured spend is $2,100 against $1,800 expected, which is 117% of pace.
Trigger: Hold because pacing remains inside the stated 85% to 120% band.

output_examples.input: A campaign spent $3,000 of $10,000 with 60% of its even flight elapsed, learning completed, and a 90% minimum pacing band.
output: Trigger: Fire and send the allocation decision to Budget Optimizer.

output_examples.input: A campaign is at 135% of pace but remains in the platform learning phase.
output: Campaign learning is still active, so the trigger remains Hold.
Review pacing again after the recorded learning-exit date.

best_practices: Set the target curve and trigger band before examining current spend.
Label each value as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Confirm learning-phase status before recommending any budget change.
anti_patterns: Do not infer daily pacing from one total or a dashboard screenshot.
Do not change the target curve after seeing current performance.
Do not present projected spend as a measured result.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide budget, flight dates, target curve, cumulative or daily spend, and learning status. Delivery fields improve cause analysis.

faq.question: Does it require an advertising platform API?
faq.answer: No. A manually exported campaign report is sufficient, while platform connectors remain optional.

faq.question: Can it calculate a new campaign allocation?
faq.answer: No. It identifies when reassessment is warranted and hands allocation work to Budget Optimizer.

faq.question: How does it handle campaigns in learning?
faq.answer: It reports pacing as observational and holds the reallocation trigger until learning has ended.

faq.question: Which target curves are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports even, front-loaded, and back-loaded curves. It defaults to even when no planned curve exists.

faq.question: How are projections presented?
faq.answer: Projected values are labeled estimated and kept separate from measured exports and user-provided inputs.
